messages:
noah: FYI jupiter reported bursts of SSE streams terminating mid-output with a 429. They get partial text and then an `event: error` with rate_limit. Ticket: https://jupiter.example/t/4521. They also pasted the response headers showing `x-quota-remaining: -2`. This is hitting prod and affects billing.

jupiter-support: paste from their capture:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
event: chunk
data: {"id":1,"text":"Hello world","tokens":45}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
event: chunk
data: {"id":2,"text":"Continuing...","tokens":30}

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
event: error
data: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"mid-stream quota"}
```
Headers on the 429: `x-request-id: rx-7f3a`, `x-quota-remaining: -2`, `retry-after: 20`. Client stack: JS SDK v0.10.1 with SSE fallback and short-lived auth tokens rotated every 45s. They say client reconnects immediately after TCP blip with a fresh token.

reena: can we grab the request ids + server-side accounting logs for rx-7f3a and any associated reconnect id? Also need `x-auth-id` mapping. If this is quota accounting related we should prioritize.

jupiter-support: they gave two request ids: `rx-7f3a` and `rx-7f3a-1` (reconnect). They say their proxy performs auth rotation automatically.

zhou: initial read of logs for rx-7f3a shows per-flush accounting entries: `acct.inc(token=tokA, +48, req=rx-7f3a)`, then on reconnect `acct.inc(token=tokB, +22, req=rx-7f3a-1)`, and then a denial when tokB falls below zero. There's also evidence that the finalize/reconcile job sometimes doesn't execute on reconnect and we never compensate the earlier estimates. That would produce a negative `x-quota-remaining`.

noah: so double-counting across token rotation is plausible. We need repro steps we can run locally to replicate reliably.

zhou: repro (server-side focused):
1) mint token A (quota 1000 units) and token B (quota 50 units)
2) client opens SSE with token A, stream emits ~900 units across a few flushes
3) simulate a network blip, client reconnects with token B immediately
4) server resumes and emits ~120 units; accounting has already charged A and now charges B -> B goes negative and 429 mid-stream
We should see logs: `acct.inc(tokA,+900)`, `acct.inc(tokB,+120)`, then `429`.

reena: code review notes: streaming pipeline increments accounting in onFlush based on estimate. There's a finalize path in onClose/onEnd to reconcile estimated vs actual, but when a reconnect occurs the old stream's finalize path doesn't run because the connection was severed before a graceful close. The reconnect creates a new stream instance and accounting ties to the presented token for that connection.

noah: quick mitigation options?

zhou: short-term: pin accounting to the initial stream session id instead of the active connection's token. We can accept an `X-Stream-Session` header from client and if absent, generate a server-side session id and return it in a `stream-session` SSE meta-event; on reconnect, if client presents the same session id we attribute charges to the original token. Shorter immediate patch: defer per-flush increments until a checkpoint (e.g., after first 3 flushes or after a heartbeat) — but that increases risk of unaccounted bursts. Prefer session-affinity server-side.

reena: are there edge cases with long-lived streams and token expiry? some customers rotate tokens for security; sessions must allow token refresh for auth but not for quota attribution. We should separate authentication from accounting: accept new token for auth but keep the accounting bucket bound to the session's original org/token-id mapping.

noah: agree. can we hotfix quickly?

deploy-bot: created branch `hotfix/stream-session-affinity-1929` and started canary deploy to staging (5% prod for smoke).

deploy-bot: canary commit b2d4a1c -> staging 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z.

jupiter-support: ran the same repro against staging with hotfix; they report no mid-stream 429 and `x-quota-remaining` looks sane. They captured staging headers: `x-quota-remaining: 28` after stream end. Good sign.

zhou: implemented mapping: on first accept we write `stream_session_id` -> `accounting_token_id` in the ephemeral store with short TTL. Reconnects with session id now map back to original token for accounting. Also made finalize step more robust (ensures reconcile runs on reconnect path and on server restart). Patches: https://git.redwood/streams/hotfix/1929 (PR open).

reena: please run an audit query for `event_type=streaming AND x-quota-remaining < 0` and `session_reconnect=true` over last 30 days so billing can review credits.

finops: will run audit after we give list of suspect orgs from logs. If there are overcharges we'll schedule credits in the next billing cycle. We need: org-id, request ids, timestamp, amount credited.

noah: I pulled 4 orgs with matching signs; two are internal test orgs and two are customers. I'll DM finops with the files.

deploy-bot: hotfix promoted main -> prod 100% at 2026-03-15T11:48:37Z.

reena: new monitoring: added metric `streams.session_reconnects_total` and `streams.duplicate_accounting_events` and a pager if duplicate_accounting_events > 0 for 5m. Also alert if `x-quota-remaining < 0` for any streaming request.

finops: audit found 3 external orgs with measurable double charges, total ~ $1,240. Credits queued; customer comms drafted.

noah: follow-ups: add e2e tests to simulate token rotation + reconnect, document recommended client behavior (prefer handing the same short-lived token for the duration of a stream, or present server-issued stream-session on reconnect), and update SDK to automatically surface `stream-session` and keep it across reconnects.

jupiter-support: customer confirms fix in prod, says they will update proxy to use session header as well once SDK update is out. Thanks for quick turnaround.

reena: I'll close the support ticket after finops confirms credits applied. Also adding a short KB note for support for similar future reports: repro steps to collect request ids, capture headers, and tell clients to present `stream-session` or avoid mid-stream token rotation.

noah: nice work. Marking resolved for Jupiter and tracking follow-ups in RT ticket 1929. :thumbsup:
